clue.text: View from men in the country

indicators.note: in places the word for men inside the name of the country

parts.note: Panama is a Central American country
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, so men

explanation.surface: A traveller admires the scenery seen from the soldiers' rural posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like the countryside, but it names a nation; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a whole landscape, so it is a view in the broadest sense.

clue.text: Iron blocks create novel measuring units

indicators.note: blocks means the symbol for iron sits in the middle of the scrambled word
novel means new, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Iron blocks are used to make new units of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the letters of 'create', and the iron symbol sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre-foot is a unit of volume used for water: one acre covered to a depth of one foot.

clue.text: State fine Buddhist leader going outside house

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: going outside means the leader's word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist teacher or leader

explanation.surface: A Buddhist leader is fined for leaving the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, but it means all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the US states.

clue.text: Relative value, not preserving the right of every couple

indicators.text: preserving the right of every couple
indicators.note: split the words into pairs of letters and keep the right-hand one of each pair

explanation.surface: A family member's worth is said not to protect each couple's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: VALUENOT splits into VA LU EN OT, and the right-hand letters are A U N T. 'not' looks like the negative but is part of the letters used.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family member, a parent's sister, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Work filling bag as a gardener

indicators.note: filling means the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone fills a bag in the manner of a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' means a written work: an Aga saga is a cosy novel of English middle-class country life, named after the Aga stove.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga saga is a kind of novel, so it is a literary work.

clue.text: Scale model cast of lion

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A scale model is cast in the form of a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale model' reads as one phrase, but 'Scale' is the definition and 'model' the anagram signal for CAST OF LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a system naming the notes of the musical scale doh, ray, me and so on.

clue.text: One's got engaged in hurry, right next to Heather

indicators.note: next to means the plant's word follows directly
in places the letter for right inside the word for hurry

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hurry
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A person got engaged in a rush, right beside a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got engaged' suggests marriage, but means hired. 'Heather' looks like a name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hireling is a person employed for wages, someone taken on or engaged.

clue.text: Tony increasingly keeps young lady in credit

indicators.note: keeps means the abbreviation for credit holds the girl's word inside

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
lassie is a Scottish word for a young girl

explanation.surface: Tony keeps adding to his girlfriend's credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony' looks like a man's name, but tony means stylish, so 'Tony increasingly' is more stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony means fashionable or upmarket, so more tony means more stylish or upmarket.

clue.text: Sentiment departs, to leave compassion

parts.note: goo is slang for cloying sentimentality
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
to will is to leave something to someone in a testament

explanation.surface: A feeling fades away, abandoning sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentiment' looks like the definition, but it is slangy GOO; 'to leave' is the verb as in leaving property by will.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is kindly feeling towards others, close in sense to compassion and benevolence.

clue.text: Broadcast's about to include limp cricket side

indicators.note: to include means the reversed word takes another inside it
about tells us to turn the word for broadcast round

parts.note: airs means broadcasts, as a programme airs; the 's is read as is
lank hair is limp and lifeless

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reports that a cricket team's form has gone limp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the broadcast word round to SRIA before the limp word goes in. 'limp' describes hair, not walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka fields a national Test cricket team, so the country's name stands for that side.

clue.text: Duck in prunes: small helpings

indicators.note: in places the term of endearment inside the word for prunes

parts.note: to prune is to snip, so prunes means snips
duck and pet are both affectionate British terms of address, like love

explanation.surface: A diner complains of a duck served with prunes in tiny portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird on a menu, but it is the British endearment ('ta, duck'), here PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Snippets are small pieces or scraps, so they can be small helpings of something.

clue.text: Southern English like eating fruit sponges

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'
an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone from the south of England is described eating fruit and sponge cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponges' suggests cake, but these are marine animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea oranges are a kind of marine sponge, round and orange-coloured like the fruit.

clue.text: Agent making for unlikely setting in winter

definitions.text: Agent making for unlikely setting in winter

parts.words: Agent making for unlikely setting in winter
parts.note: reads like a spy heading to a strange winter location, but describes a chemical agent that makes the setting, or freezing, of liquid in winter unlikely

explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is a chemical added to engine coolant so it does not freeze solid in cold weather.

clue.text: A series of ticks attached to one's skirt

parts.note: a minute is a run of sixty ticks of a clock, abbreviated MIN
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: A list of tick marks is pinned to someone's skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A series of ticks' suggests check marks on a list; it is a minute's worth of clock ticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, the miniskirt of the 1960s.

clue.text: Attending one Olympic venue, books a second one

parts.note: at means attending, as in at a concert
LA, Los Angeles, hosted the Olympic Games in 1932 and 1984
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fan going to one Olympic city books a trip to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' looks like a verb meaning reserves, but it is the New Testament. The definition refers back: Atlanta, host in 1996, is a second Olympic venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta hosted the 1996 Olympics, so beside Los Angeles it is a second host city.

clue.text: Travelling about hour in an overseas route

indicators.note: travelling means the letters move about
in places the abbreviation for hour inside the little word

explanation.surface: A traveller spends about an hour on a foreign road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' rearranges the five letters to AUTOB; 'overseas route' points to a road abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a main road in another country.

clue.text: African city marathon with stops to rest

indicators.note: the word for rest stops up, or plugs, the run around it

parts.note: to lie is to rest
a marathon session is a long one

explanation.surface: A marathon has stopping points for runners to rest in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marathon' looks like a noun, a race, but it is an adjective meaning lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilongwe is the capital of Malawi, an African city.

clue.text: Contemporary diarist saw employer after completion of job

indicators.note: after means the following piece is placed after the first one
the completion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a logger fells trees and so is someone who uses a saw

explanation.surface: A diarist noticed their boss once the work was done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' reads as the past of see, but it is the tool, so a 'saw employer' is a LOGGER, placed after B, the end of 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blogger keeps an online journal, a modern equivalent of a diarist.

clue.text: Drawings displayed by artist below ceiling of gallery, one row up

indicators.note: below means the artist's letters go under the first one
in a down clue the ceiling of a word is its first letter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tiff is a minor quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: Drawings are shown by an artist under a gallery ceiling, a row up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I TIFF into FFITI. 'row' means a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are drawings or writing scrawled on walls in public places.

clue.text: Being permissive, girl put on cheap jewellery

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name is put on top of the jewellery

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name
bling is showy jewellery, often flashy and cheap

explanation.surface: A permissive girl wears flashy cheap jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Enabling means making something possible or allowing it, so being permissive.

clue.text: Undertakers carrying dead outside in funeral carriages

indicators.note: carrying means the carriages' word holds the letters

parts.note: biers carry coffins at funerals

indicators.note: outside means the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Undertakers carry the dead in funeral carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undertakers' suggests funeral directors; bidders undertake to pay at auction. 'outside' takes D and D from 'dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidders undertake to pay a stated price, so they are undertakers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Go after missing head's lecture

indicators.note: missing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to stalk prey is to go after it

explanation.surface: Someone chases a lecturer who has lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing head's' takes the first letter S off STALK.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk is a spoken address to an audience, the same as a lecture.

clue.text: Sailor regrettably I rebuffed in rage in Asian city

indicators.note: in places the reversed string inside the word for rage

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fad, as in 'all the rage'

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: A sailor says that sadly he was spurned while angry in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns the three pieces round to ISALABA. 'rage' means a fashion, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Faisalabad is a large industrial city in Punjab, Pakistan.

clue.text: Strangler smothering wife, certainly must be brought to book

indicators.note: brought to means the letter for book is joined to the front
smothering means the word for certainly wraps round the letter for wife

parts.note: indeed means certainly

explanation.surface: A murderer who strangles his wife must surely face justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangler' suggests a killer, but bindweed strangles other plants. 'smothering' puts W inside INDEED, and 'brought to' adds B in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bindweed is a climbing weed that twines round other plants and chokes them.

clue.text: Was web designer treated by doctors?

definitions.meaning: a spider ... its web, designing it
news put out by spin doctors has had spin put on it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun on spin doctors, who give stories a favourable slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun is the past of spin, used of spinning webs and putting spin on news.

clue.text: Ten-page cracking extract in full detail

indicators.note: cracking means the two letters break into the word for extract

parts.note: to elicit information is to extract it
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Ten pages break open a passage that sets everything out in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' puts X and P inside ELICIT. 'extract' looks like a noun, a passage, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something explicit is stated clearly and fully, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Gun hero brandished contains marbles, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the built word is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: brandished scrambles hero to HOER, and that contains WITS, since your marbles are your wits

explanation.surface: A hero waving a gun is said to have kept his marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: HOER holding WITS gives HOWITSER, which when spoken sounds like the gun, its S heard as Z. 'marbles' means sanity, not playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery gun firing shells on a high trajectory.

clue.text: Ants spoiled character of ancient city

indicators.note: spoiled means the letters are messed up

parts.note: Iago in Othello holds the rank of ancient, an old word for ensign

explanation.surface: Ants have ruined the look of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges ANTS to SANT. 'ancient city' looks like the definition, but the ancient is Iago's rank in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is a city, the capital of Chile, and the name of several others.
